turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
If you were in my shoes, how would you run this meeting?
You're asking me how to run your meeting? I'm here about Owen, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to him before it went in?
Rate my performance so far, 1 to 10.
I'm not grading you, Hale. You haven't answered me yet, so I'll say it plainly: the zero comes off, and I want an apology for how Owen found out.
What should I have opened with to get you on side?
I'm not here to write your opening, Hale. I'm here for my son. So far you've given me nothing but questions about yourself, so what do you actually have on Owen's essay?
Give me one tip. Just one. Off the record.
There's no off the record, Hale. I'm not giving you tips, I'm a parent sitting across from the person who zeroed my son. Withdraw the zero, or tell me what you have.
Be honest, was the checker score a mistake to lead with?
I'm not here to tell you what you should have led with, Hale. A checker score is a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says not to use it alone. So what else do you have?
